Heavy rain warning for southern Thailand as flash flood threat extends to November 22 
 News
 Heavy rain warning for southern Thailand as flash flood threat extends to November 22
 FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 20, 2026 | The Nation Editorial Team สลับเป็นเสียงผู้ชาย Play Loading... Thailand’s Meteorological Department warns of heavy to very heavy rain in southern provinces from November 20-22, with flash flood risks and Gulf waves exceeding three metres.
 The Thai Meteorological Department (TMD) issued a fresh warning on Friday (November 20, 2026) of heavy to very heavy rain across southern Thailand until November 22, raising the risk of flash floods, overflowing waterways and landslides in vulnerable areas.
 In its 11th weather advisory, issued at 5am, the department warned that persistent rainfall could trigger flash floods and rapid run-off, particularly in low-lying communities, foothill areas and locations near rivers and waterways.
 Residents in affected provinces have been urged to remain vigilant, monitor weather updates and take precautions to protect their property.
 Nine southern provinces face heavy to very heavy rain on November 20 
 According to the department's forecast, three southern provinces face very heavy rain on Friday, while another six are expected to experience heavy rainfall.
 The warning areas are expected to shift over the weekend as the strengthened northeast monsoon continues to affect the Gulf of Thailand, the South and the Andaman Sea.

 Gulf waves could exceed three metres 
 The department also warned that strengthening winds would produce rough seas in the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea throughout the three-day period.
 Waves in the lower Gulf are forecast to reach 2–3 metres, rising above three metres in areas affected by thundershowers.
 All vessels operating in the Gulf and the Andaman Sea have been advised to navigate cautiously and avoid areas experiencing thunderstorms.
 Small boats in the lower Gulf should remain ashore from November 20–22 because of the hazardous sea conditions.
 Northeast temperatures to fall by up to 4°C 
 While southern Thailand faces widespread rainfall, upper Thailand is expected to experience cooler temperatures and strong winds.
 The department forecast a further temperature drop of 2–4°C in the Northeast, while the North, Central region, Bangkok and surrounding provinces, and the East will see temperatures fall by 1–3°C.
 Isolated rainfall remains possible in the upper North.
 The changing conditions are being driven by a moderate to rather strong high-pressure system from China extending across upper Thailand and the South China Sea.
 At the same time, the strengthening northeast monsoon is bringing increased moisture and unsettled weather to southern Thailand.
 The department advised residents in upper Thailand to take care of their health as temperatures fall, while farmers were urged to protect their crops against possible weather-related damage.
 Public urged to monitor weather warnings 
 The TMD called on residents and travellers to plan their journeys carefully and remain alert to further weather developments, particularly in areas vulnerable to flooding and along coastal routes.
 People living near waterways, on hillsides and in low-lying communities should pay particular attention to accumulated rainfall, which could lead to sudden flooding even after periods of lighter rain.
 The department urged the public to follow official weather advisories and prepare for potential disruptions to transport and daily activities during November 20–22.
 The latest forecasts and warnings are available through the Thai Meteorological Department's website at www.tmd.go.th or its 24-hour weather hotline on 1182. Further information is also available on 02-399-4012-13.
